Prose:
Scarface’s silence broke into a sharp command. He gestured toward the cell door with a jerky motion of his scarred hand, dismissing the girl’s clinging fingers as irrelevant data points in his ledger of assets. The guard obeyed instantly, the iron keyring jangling as it disengaged the primary shackles on Caelen’s wrists. The metal links fell away, leaving only loose cuffs that rattled against his forearms, a deliberate delay that felt like a cruel joke. For a heartbeat, the girl’s small hands dug into Caelen’s skin again, her nails pressing white-knuckled into the rough leather of his tunic as she refused to let go. Caelen tried to pull himself up, his broad palms scraping uselessly against the damp stone floor. Every movement felt heavier than before, gravity a stubborn anchor dragging at his limbs, but the guard’s strength was overwhelming.

They were hauled toward the door, the girl’s weeping now audible to the guards but ignored as mere background noise. She sobbed openly, her voice tearing through the silence of the cell, yet no one looked back. Caelen felt the cold indifference of the purple-robed overseer, who sat absorbed in his ledger, treating their separation as a bureaucratic formality rather than a tragedy. As they moved, the physical distance between them stretched, severing the fragile connection she represented—the only proof that someone here cared enough to cry over another. The realization settled heavily on him: shielding her had not saved her; it had made them both visible targets, transparent and vulnerable in the eyes of men who ruled by arbitrary will. The guard ignored her pleas, his boots crunching softly on gravel outside the stone walls, while Scarface watched them go with an expressionless mask, waiting to see what value they held for the auction.
